record.paper_title: Periods of Integrals on Algebraic Manifolds: Summary of Main Results and Discussion of Open Problems
record.original_question: Can the analytic or group-theoretic proof of the eigenvalue part of the monodromy theorem for a proper one-parameter degeneration be completed so that it also proves the elementary-divisor, equivalently nilpotency-index, part of the theorem for the Picard-Lefschetz transformation?

evidence.quote: Complete the proof, which is outlined in the remark below, of the eigenvalue statement of the monodromy theorem
Katz, with some valuable suggestions from Deligne, has succeeded in extending his techniques

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathcal{X}\to \Delta$ be a proper holomorphic map from a complex manifold $\mathcal{X}$ to the unit disk $\Delta\subset\mathbb{C}$, smooth over the punctured disk $\Delta^{*}=\Delta\setminus\{0\}$, with fibers $X_t = f^{-1}(t)$ smooth projective of complex dimension $n$ for $t\in\Delta^{*}$. Fix a base point $t_0\in\Delta^{*}$ and let $T:H^{k}(X_{t_0},\mathbb{Q})\to H^{k}(X_{t_0},\mathbb{Q})$ be the Picard–Lefschetz (local monodromy) transformation obtained by parallel transport along the positive generator of $\pi_1(\Delta^{*},t_0)$.

The local monodromy theorem has two parts:
(i) (Eigenvalue part) Every eigenvalue of $T$ is a root of unity; equivalently, there exist positive integers $m$ such that $T^{m}$ is unipotent.
(ii) (Elementary-divisor / nilpotency-index part) For such $m$, the unipotent operator $T^{m}$ satisfies $(T^{m}-I)^{k+1}=0$, i.e. the size of every Jordan block of $T^{m}$ is at most $k+1$, where $k$ is the cohomological degree.

Problem: Provide a proof — analytic or group-theoretic in nature — of part (i) that simultaneously yields part (ii), i.e. produces the bound $k+1$ on the index of nilpotence of $T^{m}-I$ on $H^{k}(X_{t_0},\mathbb{Q})$.
artifact.status_search_result: The local monodromy theorem, including both the quasi-unipotence (eigenvalue) part and the nilpotency-index bound on Jordan block sizes, was established by Landman (1967/1973) via Picard–Lefschetz methods, and by Katz (with input from Deligne) using p-adic/Gauss–Manin connection techniques in "Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem" (Publ. IHÉS 39, 1970), which gives the bound on the exponent of nilpotence. Analytic proofs were later given by Schmid via the nilpotent orbit theorem. The problem is regarded as solved.

status_evidence.title: Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem (Katz)
status_evidence.snippet: The main result is that in characteristic p, the Gauss-Manin connection ... is nilpotent of exponent < i+1.
status_evidence.claim: Katz proves the nilpotency-index bound, completing the elementary-divisor part of the monodromy theorem.

status_evidence.title: Monodromy (Ebeling)
status_evidence.snippet: Borel, Grothendieck, and Landman proved that T is a quasi-unipotent matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Eigenvalue and Jordan-block parts of the local monodromy theorem are established.
